messages:
ana: quick update — I ran a cross-pop onboarding benchmark for the new Llama3-small variant. Compared H100 (int8), A100 (int8), and H100 (fp16) across us-east / us-west / eu-west. p50s look fine but p95 in eu-west is unusually high. pasting highlights and raw snippets below.

ana: summary table (aggregated, avg 256 tokens request):
```
CONFIG, REGION, GPU, p50(ms), p95(ms), tok/s
H100 int8, us-east, H100, 38, 120, 320
H100 int8, us-west, H100, 42, 205, 305
H100 int8, eu-west, H100, 58, 380, 260
A100 int8, us-east, A100, 52, 140, 255
A100 int8, eu-west, A100, 71, 420, 225
H100 fp16, us-east, H100, 45, 130, 300
```

brian: looked at traces — eu-west tail aligns with an extra proxy hop and intermittent 100-300ms spikes on the edge egress. traceroute snippet showed a flaky hop at the CDN/proxy layer.

brian: traceroute (excerpt):
```
1 10.0.0.1 (10.0.0.1) 1.2 ms
2 proxy-eu-edge.myorg.net (52.16.10.4) 10.9 ms
3 transit-isp (x.x.x.x) 210.3 ms  <-- occasional large RTT
4 cluster-eu-west (10.2.1.7) 12.1 ms
```

cheng: kernel/exec notes — H100 int8 is using fused-attn-v2 kernels in us-east/us-west and we see the fastest p50s there. In eu-west our build fell back to the generic quant kernel (missing fused registration) so both throughput and tail suffer. A100 quant path still routes through the older attention fallback on all regions which explains its higher baseline p50.

cheng: quick perf note — enabling fused-attn-v2 on H100 reduced p95 by ~15% in our microbench (same shape, short seq warm). That maps to ~40-60ms p95 improvement in the numbers above if applied.

sara: quality check — ran light eval on our standard prompt set. int8 vs fp16: avg delta is small (ROUGE/QA metrics show ~0.2-0.4 drop). For Llama3-small this looks acceptable for non-SLA customers. No obvious semantic regressions.

sara: however, some eu-west requests re-run due to timeouts -> duplicates causing billing/throughput artifacts.

ana: hypothesis list:
- primary: extra edge/proxy hop in eu-west + sporadic ISP latency causing long tails.
- secondary: missing fused kernels on eu-west H100 causing CPU/GPU imbalance and longer tail under bursts.
- tertiary: cold KV cache/warmup policy plus load-balancer stickiness amplifying tails for a small subset of requests.

ana: proposed short actions (canary-first):
1) infra: enable fused-attn-v2 build on eu-west H100 canary (cheng + infra).
2) routing: add a geo-preference override for customer-critical routes to bias to us-east until eu-west stabilizes (@sre / @infra).
3) warmup: send light warmup traffic during scale-up and surface cache-miss metrics per-pop.
4) retry logic: bump internal retry timeout jitter to avoid duplicate work for borderline tails.

brian: quick capacity sizing thought — using p95 numbers and 256-token avg: assume H100 int8 sustained tok/s ~= 320 (from p50), but using p95 tail we should size to p95 throughput ~= 0.7 * p50 tok/s for safety under bursty patterns. Practically:
- safe single H100 bucket for SLA traffic ~ 220 tok/s (~70% of 320).
- for 1k concurrent 256-token requests/minute target, that maps to ~ (1000 req/min * 256 tok) / 60 = 4266 tok/s -> ~20 H100s at safety.

cheng: add-on: once fused kernel is onboarded, re-run the small sweep because p95 improvement will reduce the H100 count by ~10-15% in that calc.

ops-bot: canary deploy scheduled: eu-west/h100/fused-kernel -> 2319879000 (ETA). Monitoring: perf.p95, kv_cache_miss_rate, edge_retry_count.

ana: immediate ask: infra + eng-ml can we prioritize the fused quant wheel in eu-west canary? Also can SRE validate edge path TTLs and any ISP routing anomalies? tagging @brian @cheng @sara for owners. :rocket:

brian: will start traceroutes+pcaps and open ticket with CDN partner.

cheng: I’ll prepare the build and test microbench against canary cluster today.

sara: I’ll blacklist critical accounts from eu-west sticky routing until we have stable numbers (low friction workaround).

ana: thanks — I’ll post a short follow-up with the canary results and updated sizing once we have the fused kernel data.
